combo_label: Keys & Locks × Bell Ringing × Samurai & Feudal Japan

entries.clue: Poem of seventeen syllables, anchored by a single word naming the season
Two bells sounding at the same instant, the fault judges count
Raised wooden clog that clacks and keeps a long hem clear of mud
Venerable way of ringing on five or seven, its name an old word for a forebear
Loughborough firm, the last big caster of bells left in Britain
Warrior's code of loyalty and honour, mostly written down once the wars had ended
Theatre compartment, or the deposit sort rented in a bank strongroom
Ritual self-disembowelling by which a disgraced warrior kept his name
The chamber above the ringers, where the heavy metal actually hangs
Cabin where blades are copied, or the red sort with a telephone in it
Cut of lamb braised slowly, or the plain stem below a bow
Angled slat, one of a set filling a tower opening to let the sound out
Standing not quite shut — a door left that way invites trouble
Turn the mechanism and let the door open to anyone
